name: Spain
summary: Under the common law, children are guaranteed two thirds of the estate and a will cannot remove it. A foreign national resident can choose their national law under the EU Succession Regulation. Foral regions differ, and Spain has no trust law and no private family foundation.
reserved_share: Common Civil Code: children and descendants 2/3 (1/3 strict legitima, 1/3 free to distribute among them, art. 806-808); ascendants 1/2 or 1/3 if there is a spouse (art. 809) when there are no descendants; the spouse gets a usufruct (art. 834 ff.). Foral law differs: Catalonia 1/4 as a money claim; Navarre only a symbolic share; the Basque Country (Ley 5/2015) a collective 1/3; Aragon a collective 1/2 (regional figures from secondary guides).
foreign_law_note: Reg. 650/2012 art. 22 allows a choice of nationality law for the whole estate, which removes the legitima. For a foreigner, regional law follows habitual residence (art. 36), so the foral rules apply to foreigners living in a foral region.
trust_note: Spain has no trust law and is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention. The HCCH status table lists no signature or ratification for this state; the Convention is not in force here. Foreign trusts are not specifically regulated and are dealt with case by case for tax. Foundations (Ley 50/2002) must serve general-interest purposes and cannot mainly benefit the founder or family, so a private family foundation is not available.
open_questions: Regional legitima figures come from secondary guides and were not checked against the foral statutes.
Spanish tax treatment of foreign trusts was not researched.
Art. numbers in Ley 50/2002 on the ban on family benefit were not verified.
